1000 Genomes trio screen · a call and an assembly disagree; the raw reads decide

HG01943: a 1.09-Mb de novo duplication, and how the assembly took it apart

The trio screen calls a tandem duplication of chr2:46,970,725-48,057,041 on the chromosome HG01943 has from its mother. HPRC's trio-phased assembly of the child disagrees in structure: its maternal chromosome runs straight through the segment, and its paternal chromosome holds two parts of the segment a second time, across gaps. Taking neither as the truth, this page tests both on the reads as published - the trio's short reads, then the child's long reads, then those same reads given back to the assembly. The call holds. The assembly holds all three copies' sequence, but not where they are.

31 of 31of those reads split on HPRC's assembly too: given back to it, none runs through its maternal chromosome's copy

At a glance

What happened, in one picture

What happened in the assembly

  1. The two maternal copies collapsed into one. They are identical outside one 114-kb stretch, and no read spans a 1.09-Mb copy, so the assembler read them as one. HPRC's maternal chromosome, M, holds the segment once and runs from it straight into the right flank - while 31 HiFi reads hold the junction it lacks.
  2. Pieces of the other copy went to the father. B (369 kb) and D (300 kb) are in HPRC's paternal chromosome, though B carries 279 of the mother's own alleles and none of his, and both are base for base M. A third piece, U (230 kb, where the copies differ), has no place.
  3. They were joined in across gaps no read crosses. In the paternal chromosome B and D sit between the father's own pieces A, C and E, each across a 100-N gap - the chromosome's only four.
  4. 187 kb of the other copy, and the junction, are in no piece.
  5. The father's pieces overlap, so two stretches of his sequence are there twice (20.5 kb and 17.8 kb).

Every piece is real sequence of one of the three copies: the assembly is wrong in structure, not in sequence, and the call holds.

How this page shows it

  1. The short reads call it (section 1). 31 pairs and 6 split reads join the segment's end to its start in the child and in neither parent; depth reads 3.02 copies; the mother's allele 0.65 inside the segment, 0.50 outside.
  2. The long reads hold it, molecule by molecule (section 2). 31 HiFi reads run the segment's last base into its first - as a dot plot, each climbs to the segment's end and starts again at its start - and all 29 that can be phased are the mother's; phased depth reads 1.88 maternal copies to 0.89 paternal.
  3. The same reads, given back to the assembly, show it wrong (section 3). Realigned to HPRC's own sequence, all 31 junction reads split - 29 exactly at M's segment start and end; B takes 578 of the mother's reads and none of the father's; no read crosses any gap.
  4. The copy was made in the mother's germline, from both of her chromosomes (section 5).
How to read this page. Blue is the father's and amber the mother's, by alleles at sites that tell them apart; pink marks what is missing or differs. Dotted numbers (like 3.02) and dashed terms (like the junction) explain themselves on hover; click any of them, or any mark in a figure, to pin its details in the Inspector (on the right of a wide screen). "Show the data" boxes hold the tables behind each claim; section 7 scores each side's claims, section 8 answers the questions a reviewer will ask, and section 10 gives every source, threshold and a command to check each claim yourself.
1 · The call, in short reads

What the screen found, and what the trio's short reads say

1.1

Found by the screen, read back in the trio

The screen found k-mers of the child's absent from both parents at chr2:46,970,725 and read the trio back there (stage 4e): 6 split reads and 33 pairs whose ends face away from each other across 1,086,317 bp, in the child; none in either parent. Read again here from the trio's CRAMs: 6 split reads (MAPQ 0, 6, 21, 23, 41, 60, the same on both of a read's short sides; the pairs and the long reads anchor the junction), 31 pairs at a median MAPQ of 60, and 5 and 7 reads clipped exactly at the segment's start and end. In the father 0, 0 and 0; in the mother 0, 0 and 0.

The 1KGP SV set calls it independently from the same reads: HGSV_24204, a DUP of 1,086,317 bp at chr2:46,970,724-48,057,041, PASS, by read depth, pairs, split reads and allele balance; the child 0/1, its parents 0/0 and 0/0, and no other of its 3,202 genomes (carriers: HG01943).

1.2

The junction, to the base

The reads run the segment's last base straight into its first. The two sides share 1 base, so the join could sit one base either way - too little shared sequence for recombination between repeats; a join made by repair or by replication.

1.3

Three copies, the extra one the mother's

Bin by bin, the child's short reads read 3.02 copies inside the segment against its parents', and two outside; each parent reads two (2.00 and 2.01). At the 221 parent-opposite sites inside it the mother's allele is 0.65 of the child's reads, against 0.50 at the 163 outside: two maternal copies to one paternal. Section 2 counts both again in the long reads, read by read.

1.4

Unique sequence, not a paralog

A duplication call can come from reads that belong to another copy of a segmental duplication. Every 5-kb piece of the segment and 50 kb either side, and the 5 kb either side of each breakpoint (240 pieces), was mapped to the whole of GRCh38 (minimap2 -x asm20, secondary hits kept): all 240 map first to themselves at MAPQ 60. Only 9 match anywhere else over 1 kb at 90% identity or more - the definition segmental-duplication tracks use - and they are interspersed repeats (one family 54 places over). At the breakpoints: before the start, nothing; after the start, nothing; before the end, one 2,996-bp match (95.2%) at chr2:47,910,579-47,913,565, inside the segment; after the end, nothing. Both sides of all 31 HiFi junction reads align at MAPQ 60, the shortest side 556 bp. The junction joins two unique sequences.

1.5

Neither parent carries it

Neither parent's short reads hold a split read, a pair or a clipped read at either breakpoint (section 1.1), and each reads two copies inside the segment (2.00 and 2.01). The 1KGP set genotypes both parents 0/0. The duplication is new in the child; the mother's long reads agree (section 2.7).

2 · The long reads

What the child's HiFi reads hold, molecule by molecule

2.1

The HiFi reads across the junction

HPRC's HiFi reads of HG01943 (aligned to GRCh38 at Yale): 31 align up to chr2:48,057,041 and go on from chr2:46,970,725 on the same strand. Their two sides are 997-23,624 bp and 556-20,808 bp long, every side at MAPQ 60; they begin at 31 different places and end at 30 (two, from different instruments and strands, end at the same base) - 31 distinct molecules - and come from two instruments (Revio 16, Sequel II 15) in 5 SMRT cells. Phased by the parents' alleles over the 30 kb past the segment's start, 29 carry the mother's (4-30 of her alleles each, 535 in all), none the father's (0); 2 reach no informative site.

2.2

One junction read, as a dot plot

A dot plot needs no aligner: it marks every run of bases a read shares with a stretch of sequence, and a read that matches a stretch end to end draws one straight diagonal. Figure 4 takes one junction read - m84081_231124_031433_s4/133041701/ccs, 22,246 bp, the mother's by its alleles, its two sides the most even (10,521 and 11,738 bp) - and dots it against GRCh38 around the segment's two ends. Its diagonal climbs through the segment's last 10,521 bp to its last base, then starts again at the segment's first base and climbs on: the read holds the segment's end followed directly by its start. Against GRCh38 joined as the call says, the same read draws one unbroken diagonal.

2.3

One chromosome's worth, not a mosaic

64 reads run straight through the segment's start (33 the mother's, 31 the father's): the maternal chromosome runs into its first copy as the paternal does. 69 run through its end, where all three copies are identical and nothing can be phased. One heterozygous junction against two chromosomes' worth of straight reads at each end: 31 against 64 and 69, a constitutional duplication, not a mosaic one. 1 other read stops at either breakpoint.

2.4

Three copies, two of them maternal

Inside the segment the child's short reads read 3.02 copies against its parents, bin by bin (its own flanks taken as two: 3.04), and its HiFi reads 2.79. Where the parents' alleles phase the HiFi reads (29 bins, chr2:46,990,001-47,320,000), the mother's read 1.88 and the father's 0.89 - against 0.86 and 1.17 in the left flank's 8 phased bins, where the HiFi reads oversample the father's a little (HiFi depth swings from bin to bin; the allele shares below are the steadier count). Three copies, two of them maternal, by depth alone.

2.5

The mother's alleles count the copies

At parent-opposite sites the child's alleles count its copies by parent. Inside the segment the mother's allele reads 0.65 of the child's short reads (221 sites) and 0.68 of its HiFi reads (221); outside, 0.50 and 0.43. Two maternal copies to one paternal. Past chr2:47,291,000 the parents are never opposite homozygotes - one of the mother's haplotypes matches the father's there - and the copies are read instead at mother-only sites: the child's share of her own allele is 0 or 2/3 where its two maternal copies carry the same allele, and 1/3 where they differ, which only three copies can give.

2.6

The maternal chromosome, end to end

No read spans a 1.09-Mb copy, so no read shows the whole maternal chromosome, but each of its three joins can be read. Into the segment from the left flank: 33 maternal reads straight on - the mother's chromosome enters its first copy as the reference does. Across the junction: 29 maternal reads - one copy's end joined to the other's start, on the mother's chromosome. Out of the segment: 69 reads straight on into the right flank. No read and no caller finds any other junction over the segment (section 6). The maternal chromosome is flank, copy, junction, copy, flank: a tandem duplication in place.

2.7

Not in the mother's long reads either

The mother's nanopore reads: of her 28 reads that reach either breakpoint none carries the junction, and 10 and 10 run straight through the segment's start and end, 1 kb past each. The father has no long reads; his short reads hold none of it (section 1.5).

2.8

Other callers, the same reads

6 of Yale's 10 read-based call sets write the same junction, to within 3 bp (sniffles, pbsv, sawfish, debreak, delly, svim); none writes another junction over the segment (section 6).

2.9

The phasing checks itself

Every read's parent here rests on its alleles. Reads phased by the parent-opposite sites can be checked against the parents' own alleles they also carry, which played no part in phasing them:

Reads phased to the mother carry 2,829 of her own alleles and 10 of the father's; reads phased to the father carry 4,336 of his and 0 of hers. The phasing is sound.

3 · The assembly

What HPRC's assembly holds, tested on the same reads

3.1

What HPRC published

HPRC release 2 assembled HG01943 with hifiasm 0.19.9 in trio mode: hap1 is the paternal assembly, hap2 the maternal one. Over chr2:46,400,001-48,650,000, HPRC's Winnowmap alignment finds only CM089354.1 in the paternal assembly and CM089362.1 and JBHIIL010000075.1 in the maternal one: no other contig of either haplotype aligns anywhere in these 2.25 Mb. The paternal chromosome is one sequence with four gaps of 100 N in all (HPRC's gaps track, from its chromosome assignment), and all of them lie here.

3.2

The junction reads against the assembly

The maternal chromosome the reads hold - flank, copy, junction, copy, flank (section 2.6) - needs the segment twice in one sequence. HPRC's maternal chromosome, M, holds it once, running from the first copy's start into the second's end without the junction - the two copies read as one, the familiar collapse of identical copies. The second copy's sequence is there, in pieces: B (CM089354.1, chr2:46,971,835-47,340,686) in the paternal scaffold; U (JBHIIL010000075.1, chr2:47,426,809-47,656,968) unplaced; D (CM089354.1, chr2:47,755,434-48,055,872) in the paternal scaffold.

Put to the assembly, the junction read of figure 4 meets the break it meets on GRCh38. Against M it climbs to M's segment end and starts again at M's segment start, 1.09 Mb back along M: M holds the segment once. Against the paternal chromosome its two parts land on the other copy's pieces nearest the junction - its first part runs along D to D's last base, beside gap 4, and its second starts only at B's first base, beside gap 1 - and the 2,279 bp between them, across the junction, are in no piece of that copy. Joined as the call says, M's own bases take the read end to end on one diagonal.

Every junction read says the same once realigned to HPRC's sequence (section 3.3): 29 split into a part ending at M's segment end and a part starting at its start; the other 2 hold their short side (556 and 1,657 bp) equally well on a father's piece, where the three copies share their sequence; none runs straight through either of M's segment ends.

3.3

Every read, given back to the assembly

The plainest test of an assembly is to give it back its reads. Every one of the child's 6,765 HiFi reads over the window was aligned to HPRC's own sequence over the locus - its paternal chromosome CM089354.1:46,805,838-49,047,195, the four gaps' 100 N included, its maternal chromosome CM089362.1:46,777,285-48,308,368 and the unplaced contig JBHIIL010000075.1, whole - all three at once (minimap2 -x map-hifi), so that each read takes its best place anywhere in the assembly. The sequence is the published FASTA's, read by region; it is base for base what HPRC's alignment records hold, but for 8 bases beside gap 3 that no record holds. Each read keeps the parent its alleles gave it on GRCh38.

The father's reads never reach B: 578 of the mother's reads align to it and none of his - though B sits in his chromosome. Over D's stretch the father's copy nearly matches the mother's, so few sites tell them apart: of D's 504 reads 2 are the mother's, none the father's, and the rest unphased - its sequence settles D instead (section 3.4). Every read on B and D aligns at MAPQ 0: they are base for base M, so each of the mother's reads there has two equally good places and the aligner picks one at random. That is also why depth alone sees nothing wrong: between them, M and B hold two copies' reads at one copy's depth each. Where no piece holds the other copy, M takes two copies' reads (pink), and C one stretch of them, where NucFlag calls a collapse.

No read crosses a gap. At each one, the reads that run straight through its two points on GRCh38 align elsewhere in the assembly, unbroken: of the 80 through A's end, 23 align on C - which holds the father's sequence past A's end - and 57 on M; of the 94 through B's start, 30 align on A and 64 on M. Within 2 kb of each gap's edges the depth falls to 0.01-0.09 of one haplotype's: what NucFlag reads as a misjoin.

3.4

Whose is each piece?

Trio phasing put each contig in a haplotype by the parents' k-mers. The parents' alleles check it independently. Of the 2,928 SNVs the trio's short reads call over the window, 384 are parent-opposite, 861 mother-only and 541 father-only. Read in pairs, the pieces say what each copy holds. The father's and the mother's chromosomes differ by 1.58 per kb over chr2:46,950,725-47,340,307 (A against M) and by 0.07 over chr2:47,756,575-48,077,041 (E against M), where one of the mother's haplotypes nearly matches the father's. U - the unplaced piece - differs from M at 130 places, 114 of them inside the stretch and 12 in the patchy kilobases before it: it is the other maternal copy there, as the alleles say (section 5).

3.5

The four joins, on GRCh38

A join is a claim that two pieces are neighbours. Here every join also jumps back along GRCh38: the scaffold reads a stretch it has already read. The child's HiFi reads test each:

No read crosses any join. At each of their points the reads - 79-99 - run straight on, as the reference does; a handful are clipped near a point (2, 2, 1, 1 at the four joins), and none of those goes on at the join's other point.

3.6

Copies held twice, and missing

Over the segment's 10-kb bins the assembly holds 3 copies in 87, 2 in 19 and 4 in 3 (pink in figure 5); the reads hold 3 throughout. The 4s are two false duplications where the father's pieces overlap: A and C over chr2:47,319,800-47,340,307 (20,508 bp): 0 SNVs, 6 indels; C and E over chr2:47,756,575-47,774,341 (17,767 bp): 0 SNVs, 0 indels - the same paternal sequence twice in one haplotype.

The 2s are where the second maternal copy is missing: no piece of it holds chr2:47,340,687-47,426,808 (86 kb) or chr2:47,656,969-47,755,433 (98 kb). In all 186,866 bp of it is in no piece - those stretches, the kilobase either side of the junction (B starts 1,110 bp after the segment's start, D ends 1,169 bp before its end) and the junction itself. The missing copy's reads must still align somewhere, to whatever assembled sequence they match best. Over chr2:47,340,687-47,426,808 they match M at 100 of 100 informative sites (C at 1 of 100): M should hold two copies' reads there. Over chr2:47,656,969-47,755,433, where the maternal copies differ, they match C at 53 of 55 sites and M at only 28 of 55: C should hold them, and NucFlag calls a collapse on C at chr2:47,686,528-47,711,595, inside it.

3.7

What HPRC's own QC says

HPRC's QC tracks split. NucFlag, which reads the child's reads against the assembly, calls a MISJOIN over every join, a COLLAPSE inside C and MISJOINs at both ends of U. Flagger marks only the gap bases themselves (NNN) and leaves every piece unflagged - and it has no reason to flag them: each piece is real sequence, the assembly holds the right number of copies over most of the segment, and coverage cannot see that a piece sits in the wrong chromosome. Neither tool flags M over chr2:47,340,687-47,426,808, where by the same reasoning it holds two copies' reads.

4 · What happened, step by step

From the genome to the assembly, step by step

Put together, the reads and the assembly tell one story, step by step (figure 1 draws it). Each step names its evidence; what the published data cannot show is said at the end.

  1. The genome. The mother's chromosome carries the segment twice in tandem, joined at the junction; the father's carries it once (sections 1 and 2). The two maternal copies are identical except over the 114 kb of the stretch (section 5), and over the segment's last 300 kb the father's copy nearly matches the mother's (E against M: 0.07 differences per kb).
  2. The contigs. The gap-free stretches of the released sequences are the assembler's contigs: in hap1 A, B, C, D and E; in hap2 M (one contig, through the whole segment) and U. Between them they hold the father's copy (A, C, E), one maternal copy (M) and pieces of the second (B, U, D) - three copies, as the reads say, but the second maternal copy in fragments that stop short of the junction and of each other.
  3. The phasing. B and D went into the father's haplotype although B carries 279 of the mother's own alleles and none of his, and both are base for base the maternal chromosome. Trio phasing sorts reads by parental k-mers; why these two contigs landed in hap1 the published files cannot show (section 8 weighs one explanation).
  4. The placement. In CM089354.1 the hap1 contigs lie in the order of their starts on GRCh38, joined by 100-N gaps - the only four in it. So each maternal piece falls between two paternal ones, and each join jumps back along GRCh38 by the length of the stretch read twice (368,472, 20,886, 18,907, 299,297 bp). U, in hap2, has no place.
  5. What is missing. 187 kb of the second maternal copy and the junction are in no piece. Their reads align to M or C, whichever they match (section 3.6), where NucFlag sees one collapse.
  6. Downstream. Call sets made from the assembly read the scaffold literally: PAV writes four insertions on hap1, cuteSV-asm four duplications, SVision-pro-asm breakends at the joins - the event on the wrong parent's chromosome, in four (section 6).

What the published data cannot show: the assembly graph and the contigs before chromosome assignment (the reads only show that the joins are not adjacencies); any contig that aligns nowhere in these 2.25 Mb; and hifiasm's reasons for putting B and D in hap1.

5 · Where the copy was made

Two maternal copies, not one copied twice

The mother is heterozygous at 382 mother-only sites inside the segment. At 118 of them before chr2:47,590,351 and 133 after chr2:47,704,313 the child's two maternal copies carry the same allele. But from chr2:47,590,351 to chr2:47,704,313 they differ at 111 of 117 sites: one copy carries her other chromosome there. Outside that stretch they differ at 9 sites, all in the 95 kb before it (chr2:47,495,696-47,586,996), as patches between agreeing sites.

Why that places the copy in the mother
  1. At a mother-only site the father has one allele; the child's paternal copy carries it.
  2. A share of 1/3 for her own allele means exactly one of the child's three copies carries it: one maternal copy has it, the other does not.
  3. The child received one maternal chromosome. A copy made after conception would repeat it: two identical copies, but for a few new mutations - not 111 differing sites of hers in 114 kb.
  4. So the two maternal copies were made from both of the mother's chromosome 2s: in her germline.

Her nanopore reads phase her heterozygous sites into her two haplotypes, in blocks as long as her reads link them (47,059,845-47,106,698, 28 sites; 47,163,438-47,385,570, 122 sites; 47,557,874-47,730,934, 177 sites; 47,768,911-48,146,937, 163 sites; no read contradicts a link). The block from chr2:47,557,874 to chr2:47,730,934 spans the whole stretch. Read against it, the child's two maternal copies carry her haplotype 2 before the stretch (15 sites; in the patchy kilobases 7 read both haplotype 1 and 8 one of each), one of each inside it (109 of 115 sites), and her haplotype 1 after it (22 of 22). Each copy changes from her haplotype 2 to her haplotype 1, at a different place: one near chr2:47,590,351, the other between chr2:47,704,313 and chr2:47,713,612.

Two copies that leave one of her chromosomes for the other at different places are two chromatids that had each exchanged with her other chromosome - something meiosis does - joined by the duplication. Two exchanges 123 kb apart in one meiosis are unusual; a copy made by a process that switched templates partway, as replication-based duplications with no shared sequence at the junction often do, would account for one of them. Either way the extra copy was made in her germline, from both of her chromosomes. Which copy is first the reads cannot say: the stretch lies 329 kb from the nearest junction read's end. The assembly saw the difference too: over the stretch M carries one copy's alleles and U the other's.

7 · Each claim, scored

What each side claims, and what would undo it

The call: HG01943 carries a de novo tandem duplication of chr2:46,970,725-48,057,041 (1,086,317 bp) on the chromosome from its mother: the segment twice, its end (chr2:48,057,041) joined to its start (chr2:46,970,725).
The assembly (HPRC release 2, hifiasm 0.19.9, trio-phased): the maternal chromosome CM089362.1 holds the segment once, straight through. The paternal chromosome CM089354.1 holds it in five pieces, A, B, C, D, E, joined across four 100-N gaps, and reads chr2:46,971,835-47,340,686 and chr2:47,755,434-48,055,872 twice. A 230,135-bp maternal contig, JBHIIL010000075.1, aligns inside the segment and has no chromosome position.

The review read this as one to follow up: at a duplication, a haplotype that runs straight through, or cannot be read, never counts against a call, because copies collapse in assemblies - and a call can be wrong too. Each side makes claims the raw reads can test. The trio's short reads, the child's HiFi reads and the mother's nanopore reads, as published, were read for each of them, and the child's reads were given back to the assembly itself:

What would undo the call

  • junction reads that belong to a paralog, or are chimeras
  • two copies by depth, or alleles at 1/2
  • the extra copy the father's
  • the junction in a parent's reads
  • other callers on the same reads finding something else

What would bear out the assembly

  • reads crossing each of the scaffold's four joins
  • its own reads, given back to it, fitting it unbroken
  • pieces B and D carrying the father's alleles
  • no read holding the junction
  • the copies it holds matching the reads' count, bin by bin
  • its QC tracks calling it sound

The call: the junction in the short reads

Holds. 6 split reads and 31 read pairs join chr2:48,057,041 to chr2:46,970,725 in the child; none in either parent. The 1KGP set calls the duplication too, in the child alone. More

The call: a paralog?

Holds. Every 5-kb piece of the segment and its flanks (240) maps first to itself in GRCh38 at MAPQ 60; neither breakpoint lies in a segmental duplication; the two sides share 1 bp. More

The call: three copies

Holds. Short reads 3.02 copies against the parents, bin by bin; HiFi 2.79; each parent 2.00 and 2.01. More

The call: the extra copy the mother's

Holds. The mother's allele 0.65 inside (221 parent-opposite sites), 0.50 outside; phased HiFi reads 1.88 maternal copies to 0.89 paternal. More

The call: the HiFi junction reads

Holds. 31 reads from two instruments, both sides at MAPQ 60; 29 of 29 phasable carry the mother's alleles, none the father's. More

The call: other callers on the same reads

Holds. 6 of Yale's 10 read-based call sets write the same junction, to within 3 bp. More

The assembly: the scaffold's joins

Fails. None of the 4 joins is crossed by a HiFi read; 79-99 run straight through each point. NucFlag calls a misjoin at each. More

The assembly: its reads, given back

Fails. Realigned to HPRC's own sequence, all 31 junction reads split, none running through its maternal chromosome's copy; B takes 578 of the mother's reads and none of the father's. More

The assembly: whose pieces

Fails. Pieces B and D of the paternal scaffold carry the mother's own alleles and none of the father's, and match the maternal chromosome base for base. More

The assembly: the copies

Fails. Over the segment the assembly holds 3 copies in 87 of its 10-kb bins, 2 in 19 and 4 in 3; the reads hold 3 throughout. More

The assembly: its own QC

Fails. NucFlag flags every join and a collapse; Flagger flags only the gap bases. More

8 · A reviewer's questions

The questions an expert will ask, answered from this page

Could the junction reads be chimeras or one library's artifact?
They are 31 distinct molecules - 31 different starts, 30 different ends (two, from different instruments and strands, share one) - from two instruments (Revio 16, Sequel II 15) and 5 SMRT cells, and every one joins the same two bases. Both sides of each align at MAPQ 60, each at least 556 bp long. The short reads (6 split, 31 pairs) and the 1KGP set find the same junction independently.
Could it be reads mapped to the wrong copy of a repeat?
Every 5-kb piece of the segment maps first to itself in GRCh38 at MAPQ 60, and neither breakpoint lies in sequence repeated elsewhere (section 1.4). The junction k-mers are absent from both parents. And the signal is not only at the breakpoints: depth and alleles read three copies along the whole 1.09 Mb.
How sure is it that the extra copy is the mother's?
Four independent ways: the mother's allele reads 0.65 inside at 221 parent-opposite sites; phased HiFi depth reads 1.88 maternal copies to 0.89 paternal; every phasable junction read (29) is the mother's; and at mother-only sites the child's share of her allele is 2/3 or 1/3 (two maternal copies), never 1/2.
Is it really de novo, and constitutional?
Neither parent's short reads hold a split read, pair or clip at the breakpoints; they read 2.00 and 2.01 copies; none of the mother's 28 nanopore reads at the breakpoints carries the junction; the 1KGP set genotypes both 0/0 and calls no other carrier. In the child the junction is carried at one chromosome's rate (31 reads against 64 and 69 straight through the ends) and depth reads 3.02 copies, not the 2.5 a half-mosaic would give.
Why does the maternal chromosome run straight through, and why is the junction in no contig?
The two maternal copies are identical except over the stretch (they agree at 251 of the mother's het sites outside it), so a path through one copy into the right flank is as consistent with the reads as one through both. The pieces of the second copy stop 1,110 bp and 1,169 bp short of the junction, and no contig of either haplotype that aligns over these 2.25 Mb holds it. That is a collapse of identical copies with a fragmented remainder.
Is the assembly's sequence wrong, or only its structure?
Only its structure. B and D are base for base the maternal chromosome; U differs from M only where the copies themselves differ (126 of its 130 differences inside the stretch or the patchy kilobases before it); Flagger flags no piece. Every allele the reads find is in some piece.
Why would hifiasm put maternal contigs in the paternal haplotype?
The published files cannot show its graph. One explanation for experts to weigh: the second maternal copy is identical to the first over most of its length, so its reads double the mother's depth there (phased HiFi 1.88 maternal copies) - the depth of sequence both haplotypes share, which a haplotype-resolved assembler puts in both. B nonetheless carries 279 of the mother's own alleles and none of the father's, so k-mers alone should have marked it maternal.
Did the assembler or the scaffolding make the joins?
The joins are runs of 100 N - no sequence crosses them, so no read could have built them. They are the paternal chromosome's only gaps (HPRC's gaps track, from its chromosome assignment), and its pieces are ordered by their start on GRCh38. The contigs came from the assembler; their order and the joins came at chromosome assignment.
Is giving the reads back to the assembly fair to it?
It gives the assembly every chance: all 6,765 primary HiFi reads of the GRCh38 window, aligned to both of HPRC's chromosomes and the unplaced contig at once with the standard HiFi preset, so that a read the assembly can hold anywhere in the locus finds that place. The sequence is HPRC's published FASTA, read by region; the segment is unique in GRCh38 (section 1.4), so no read from elsewhere belongs here. The reads keep the parents their alleles gave them on GRCh38.
Why are all of B's and D's reads at MAPQ 0?
B and D are base for base M, so every read that fits one fits the other equally well; the aligner places each at random between them and says so with MAPQ 0. Between them M and B (or M and D) hold two copies' reads at one copy's depth each - right for depth, wrong for haplotype: only the mother's reads ever land on B.
Do the dot plots depend on an aligner?
No. A run of identical 16-base words in the read and the window is a segment, drawn where it lies; runs under 40 bp are left out, so that repeats' short matches do not clutter the picture. A read that matches a stretch end to end draws one straight diagonal; where it stops matching, the diagonal stops, and goes on elsewhere or nowhere.
Why does Flagger not flag any of it, while NucFlag does?
Flagger judges each base by read depth. Each piece is real sequence read at the depth its copy implies, so coverage looks right except over the gap bases (NNN). A piece in the wrong chromosome changes no base's depth. NucFlag looks at the pileup's breaks: near every join the depth falls toward zero - the reads that would cross it align elsewhere, unbroken (section 3.3) - which it calls MISJOIN, and reads pile onto C where the missing copy's reads land (COLLAPSE).
Is the 1/3 share of the mother's allele a mapping or genotyping artifact?
The HiFi and short reads agree site by site (section 5's table); the sites lie in unique sequence; the mother is heterozygous at each by her own short reads (each allele in a fifth of her reads or more); and the stretch is contiguous - 111 of 117 sites - with the assembly's two maternal pieces differing there too (M against U).
Could the mother's phase be wrong, and the switches an artifact of it?
The core does not depend on her phase: the copies differ inside the stretch and agree on either side, so at each end one copy must change haplotype whatever her phase says. Her phase only says which copy, and in which direction. It is built from her own reads with no conflicting link (768 linked reads), and at the right end the change is seen inside single HiFi molecules (10 go from her haplotype 2 to 1, none the other way).
Why is the HiFi depth 2.79 copies, not 3?
HiFi depth varies more than short-read depth along a 1-Mb stretch, and there is no parental HiFi to divide by. The phased depth, which cancels it, reads 1.88 maternal to 0.89 paternal copies: two to one. In the left flank the HiFi reads oversample the father a little: the mother's allele reads 0.43 of them at the parent-opposite sites there, against 0.50 of the short reads - so the HiFi shares understate the mother's, if anything.
What can the data not tell?
Which maternal copy is first; the exact sequence of the 187 kb the assembly lacks (the reads hold it, but it was not assembled here); whether a contig that aligns nowhere in this window holds the junction; and the mechanism - meiotic exchange or template switching.
9 · Verdict, and the review

Which side is wrong

The call stands; the assembly is wrong in structure, not in sequence. The call passes every test that could have undone it, in the short reads and in the long. The assembly fails its own reads, given back to it: every junction read splits on it. It holds all three copies' sequence, but places two maternal pieces in the father's chromosome across joins no read supports, leaves a third without a place, and lacks 187 kb of the second copy and the junction.

For the review's rules on large duplications - proposed here, not applied:

  • Rule 3 held. At a duplication, a haplotype that runs straight through, or cannot be read, is borderline and never against the call. Counted against, as at a deletion, it would have failed a true 1.09-Mb de novo duplication. Keep it.
  • A haplotype that reads the segment twice across gaps is a sign, not a blank. The traversal could read the pieces' parents by the trio's alleles (a piece of the other parent's marks a misplaced copy) and count the copies both haplotypes hold, unplaced contigs included, against the call's copy number.
  • A join across N is never evidence. The review already treats it so; the assembly-based call sets do not. A call at an assembly gap should count for nothing.
  • Phased long-read depth settles copy number where junction reads cannot. A long-read line for large duplications could add it.
  • This card's follow-up has an answer. It could be marked followed up, with a link to this page.

Every threshold

whatrule
sitesbiallelic SNVs, QUAL 30 or more; each parent's depth within half and twice its median; a homozygous call with at most one read (or 5%) of the other allele, a heterozygous one with a fifth of the reads each way
mapping quality20 for every read, short or long
a junction in a long readone alignment ending within 50 bp of a point with 100 or more bases clipped, another on the same strand starting within 50 bp of the other point, clipped; at the scaffold's joins within 1000 bp
straight through a pointone alignment 1000 bp either side
a read's parent2 or more parent-opposite sites, 4 in 5 agreeing; else 2 or more of one parent's own alleles and none of the other's; alleles within 30 kb of a breakpoint for the junction reads
depthsamtools bedcov in 10-kb bins at MAPQ 20; each member's flanks = the bins more than 10 kb outside the segment
the copies at a mother-only site20 or more HiFi reads; her own allele's share under 1/6 = 0, to 0.42 = 1/3, to 0.58 = 1/2 (neither), to 0.83 = 2/3
the stretchthe longest run of 'differ' sites, merged across at most two 'agree' sites
the mother's phaseevery pair of her heterozygous sites on one of her reads (MAPQ 20) votes; a link needs 3 or more reads, 85% agreeing; links joined strongest first
uniquenessminimap2 -x asm20 -c -N 100 -p 0.05 --secondary=yes against the whole analysis set; a match elsewhere counts over 1 kb at 90% identity
pieces against each othereach record's SNVs and indels against GRCh38 from its CIGAR and sequence; two pieces' differences over the stretch both cover
a parent's piece3 or more of one parent's own alleles inside the segment, and 2% or fewer of the other's
reads given back to the assemblyevery primary HiFi read of the GRCh38 window (6,765, any MAPQ) aligned with minimap2 -ax map-hifi --eqx -Y to HPRC's published sequence over the locus: the paternal and maternal chromosomes over the window and 100 kb either side, and the unplaced contig whole; each read keeps the parent its alleles gave it on GRCh38; depth in 5-kb bins, primary and supplementary alignments, in copies of one haplotype's depth (the left flank's, beyond 10 kb of the segment: 41.2x paternal, 33.6x maternal, 37.4x their mean)
a junction read on the assemblyan alignment ending within 50 bp of M's segment end with 100 or more bases clipped, another starting within 50 bp of its start, clipped; straight through either = one alignment 1000 bp either side
a read across a gapan alignment ending within 1000 bp of a gap's left edge with 100 or more bases clipped and another starting within 1000 bp of its right edge, clipped; depth at a gap's edge = the 2 kb beside it
dot plotsexact 16-base words shared by the read (in GRCh38's orientation) and each window, both strands, chained into runs along each diagonal; runs of 40 bp or longer drawn; the read: the mother's junction read with the most even sides, both at MAPQ 60; at join 1 the father's read straight through A's end and the mother's through B's start, 1 kb or more either side, with the longest shorter side

Terms

The segment
chr2:46,970,725-48,057,041 (GRCh38), the 1,086,317 bp the call says is duplicated.
The junction
Where the segment's last base (chr2:48,057,041) meets its first (chr2:46,970,725): the join a tandem duplication makes between its two copies.
A copy
One instance of the segment on a chromosome. The reads hold three: the father's and two of the mother's.
Parent-opposite site
A SNV where one parent is homozygous for one allele and the other parent for the other. Any read's parent can be read off it.
Mother-only site
A SNV where only the mother is heterozygous (the father homozygous): her second allele is hers alone. At such a site the child's share of it counts its maternal copies carrying it: 0, 1/3 or 2/3 of three copies.
Father-only site
A SNV where only the father is heterozygous: his second allele is his alone.
A parent's own allele
An allele the other parent does not carry: at a parent-opposite site, each parent's; at a mother-only site, her second allele; at a father-only site, his.
A piece
A gap-free stretch of one of HPRC's assembled sequences, as HPRC's own alignment to GRCh38 (Winnowmap) records it over the segment. A-E lie in the paternal chromosome scaffold, M is the maternal chromosome, U an unplaced maternal contig.
A join
Where two pieces of the paternal scaffold meet across a run of 100 N: the scaffold's claim that the two pieces are neighbours on the chromosome.
A gap (100 N)
A run of 100 N in an assembled sequence: the conventional mark for neighbours at an unknown distance. No sequence, so no read can support or refute it directly; reads can only show whether the two sides meet.
hap1 / hap2
The assembly's two haplotypes: hap1 is HG01943's paternal assembly (HG01943_pat_hprc_r2_v1.0.1), hap2 its maternal one, separated by hifiasm using k-mers found only in the father's, or only in the mother's, short reads (trio phasing).
Her haplotype 1 / 2
The mother's two chromosome 2s, phased here from her own nanopore reads, block by block. The labels 1 and 2 hold within a block only.
The stretch
chr2:47,590,351-47,704,313, where the child's two maternal copies differ: one carries the mother's other chromosome there.
Phased read
A read assigned to a parent by its alleles: two or more parent-opposite sites, four in five agreeing; else two or more of one parent's own alleles and none of the other's.
MAPQ
Mapping quality: the aligner's confidence that a read belongs where it is placed, on a log scale; 60 is the most confident, a unique placement.
NucFlag
An HPRC QC tool that aligns the child's HiFi reads back to its assembly and calls places where the read pileup breaks (MISJOIN), holds more than one copy's reads (COLLAPSE) or shows two alleles (HET).
Flagger
HPRC's coverage HMM: it labels each assembled base erroneous, falsely duplicated, haploid (as expected) or collapsed by its read depth, and gap bases NNN. The tracks read here list every label but haploid.
Trio phasing
hifiasm's mode that sorts reads (and the assembly graph) into the father's and the mother's haplotype by k-mers seen in only one parent's short reads.
Chromosome assignment
HPRC's step that names each haplotype's chromosome-scale sequences (here CM089354.1 and CM089362.1); its gaps track lists the 100-N runs in them.
Winnowmap alignment
HPRC's published alignment of each assembled haplotype to GRCh38 (Winnowmap 2): one record per aligned piece, with its contig coordinates.
SMRT cell
One PacBio sequencing run. Read names start with the instrument and cell: m64043 a Sequel II, m84081 a Revio.
HiFi reads
PacBio circular-consensus reads, here a median of 18.6 kb long and about 99.9% accurate; HPRC's reads of the child, aligned to GRCh38 at Yale.
The mother's nanopore reads
Oxford Nanopore reads of HG01942 from the 1000 Genomes ONT project (Vienna), about 15x here, a median of 3.6 kb long.
Constitutional
Present in every cell, not in a fraction of them (mosaic).
False duplication
One haplotype's sequence held twice in an assembly.
Collapse
Two or more copies in the genome held once in the assembly; their reads pile onto the one copy.
Copies (depth)
Read depth over a bin divided by the depth of the flanks and multiplied by two: two copies outside the event, three over a heterozygous duplication.
Split read
A read aligned in two parts, one at each side of a junction.
Discordant pair
A read pair whose two ends face away from each other across the segment, as pairs across a tandem duplication's junction do.
The 1KGP SV set
The 1000 Genomes high-coverage short-read structural-variant call set (GATK-SV with svtools and MELT, NYGC freeze V3), over the same 30x reads.
Dot plot
Two sequences against each other: x the read, y a stretch of reference or assembly. Every run of identical 16-base words the two share is drawn where it lies (40 bp or longer here). A read that matches a stretch end to end draws one straight diagonal; where it stops matching, the diagonal stops - and goes on elsewhere, or nowhere. No aligner is involved.
Reads given back to the assembly
The child's HiFi reads over the window aligned again (minimap2 -x map-hifi), to HPRC's own published sequence over the locus - both chromosomes and the unplaced contig at once - instead of GRCh38, so that each read takes its best place in the assembly.
Yale's call sets
16 call sets of HG01943 Yale made for HPRC release 2: 10 from its HiFi reads, 5 from its assembly, 1 merged.
